LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.6: Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing, part of Writing in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is greeting important? 2. How does spelling ensure language accuracy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the common spelling mistakes in writing of Arabic words related to greetings and introductions,

2. write words with letter baa, lam, mim, daal correctly,

3. work jointly to fill gaps in words with missing Arabic characters,

4. work jointly to form words related to the theme from a collection of jumbled up characters in Arabic,

5. copy the Arabic greetings phrases neatly and legibly,

6. team up to practice greetings with peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the common spelling mistakes in writing of Arabic words related to greetings and introductions,
2. write words with letter baa, lam, mim, daal correctly,
3. work jointly to fill gaps in words with missing Arabic characters,
4. work jointly to form words related to the theme from a collection of jumbled up characters in Arabic,
5. copy the Arabic greetings phrases neatly and legibly,
6. team up to practice greetings with peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts when forming words related to the

theme from a collection of jumbled up characters in Arabic.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows concerted attention when writing words with letter baa, lam, mim, daal

using correct spelling.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner teams up with peers to practise greetings with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Gender issues: These are addressed as the learner appreciate their own and the opposite gender when practicing various

greetings and introductions while working in groups or pairs.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on greetings and introductions to similar concepts covered in English.
